name: Lunar Gateway
operator: NASA-led with ESA, JAXA, CSA, MBRSC (UAE)
short_status: Paused in its current form since Mar 24, 2026; HALO under stop-work, PPE repurposed for the SR-1 Freedom Mars mission, partners re-planning (as of Jul 18, 2026)
tagline: NASA and partners · Multinational · Programme · 2017 · Commercial and multipolar In development
stats: farthest point of Gateway's planned halo orbit above the Moon
solar electric power of the PPE, now bound for Mars instead
HALO contract value at the April 2026 stop-work, up from $935M in 2021
partner agencies left re-planning: ESA, JAXA, CSA and the UAE's MBRSC

facts.label: Organisations
facts.value: NASA-led with ESA, JAXA, CSA, MBRSC (UAE)

facts.label: Concept unveiled
facts.value: 2017, as the Deep Space Gateway; renamed Lunar Orbital Platform-Gateway in 2018, then simply Gateway in 2019

facts.label: PPE contract
facts.value: Awarded 23 May 2019 to Maxar Technologies; total value including options $375 million

facts.label: PPE spec
facts.value: 60-kilowatt solar electric propulsion spacecraft supplying Gateway's power, communications and orbit control

facts.label: Launch contract
facts.value: 9 Feb 2021: SpaceX Falcon Heavy to launch PPE and HALO together from LC-39A, approx $331.8 million, then targeted no earlier than May 2024

facts.label: HALO contract
facts.value: $935 million firm-fixed-price finalized with Northrop Grumman on 9 July 2021; design derived from the Cygnus cargo ship

facts.label: Planned orbit
facts.value: Near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), roughly 7-day period, about 3,000 km over the north pole at closest and 70,000 km at farthest

facts.label: International elements
facts.value: ESA: Lunar I-Hab (with JAXA life support), Lunar View, Lunar Link; CSA: Canadarm3; MBRSC (UAE): Crew and Science Airlock, announced 7 Jan 2024

facts.label: HALO arrives in US
facts.value: 1 April 2025 at Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport, after primary-structure fabrication by Thales Alenia Space in Turin; moved to Northrop Grumman's Gilbert, Arizona facility for outfitting

facts.label: Corrosion problem
facts.value: After the 2025 delivery, Northrop Grumman found widespread corrosion throughout HALO's primary structure; Northrop's own estimated delivery slipped to July 2028, and NASA's OIG projected that had work continued, HALO would not have been delivered until about July 2031, with Gateway not operational until at least 2032 (counterfactual projections; no plan ever carried these dates)

facts.label: Contract growth
facts.value: HALO grew from a $935M fixed-price deal (2021) to a cost-plus contract at $1.8B (Sept 2024) and $1.9B by the April 2026 stop-work order

facts.label: The pause
facts.value: 24 March 2026, at the "Ignition" rollout: Administrator Jared Isaacman said NASA "intends to pause Gateway in its current form and shift focus to infrastructure that enables sustained surface operations"

facts.label: Stop-work chain
facts.value: NASA issued a HALO stop-work order in April 2026; in June 2026 Northrop Grumman told its HALO subcontractors to stop work and reassigned staff

facts.label: OIG accounting
facts.value: 24 June 2026 OIG interim memo (Report No. ML-26-002): combined contract values for four canceled Artemis elements (HALO, Mobile Launcher 2, Exploration Upper Stage, Universal Stage Adapter) ballooned from nearly $2.8B to $5.9B, with delivery dates extended by up to 7 years and estimated completion costs of at least $8.1B; the widely cited 'over $5.3B in overruns' is analyst Douglas Messier's derivation from those numbers, a total the memo itself never prints

facts.label: PPE's new life
facts.value: The PPE becomes the electric-propulsion bus of Space Reactor-1 Freedom, announced 24 March 2026 and billed by NASA as humanity's first fission-powered interplanetary spacecraft: 20 kWe Brayton-cycle reactor, 12-kW Hall thruster, launch targeted for late 2028 (as of 28 September 2026); whether it flies by Mars or enters orbit was undecided at announcement

facts.label: PPE builder
facts.value: Lanteris Space Systems, the former Maxar Space Systems; Intuitive Machines completed its $800M acquisition of Lanteris on 13 Jan 2026

facts.label: ESA disposition
facts.value: 17 June 2026 ESA Council: Lunar I-Hab continues through critical design review then repurposing assessment; Lunar View slows down; Lunar Link studied as a standalone comms asset or part of ESA's Moonlight constellation; roadmap decisions due at the interim ministerial ESA has set for December 2026 in Italy

facts.label: Canada's position
facts.value: CSA's Canadarm3 contract with MDA Space is unchanged; MDA says the robotic arm, still in design phase, can pivot to low Earth orbit, cislunar or lunar surface roles

facts.label: UAE's position
facts.value: MBRSC reaffirmed its commitment to Artemis and its NASA partnership after the pause (March 2026)

facts.label: Artemis renumbering
facts.value: Under the architecture NASA announced on 27 February 2026, a month before the Gateway pause, Artemis III became an Earth-orbit integrated test in 2027 and the crewed lunar landings moved to Artemis IV and V

timeline: NASA unveils the concept as the Deep Space Gateway
Maxar wins the Power and Propulsion Element contract ($375M including options)
Oct 2020
NASA and ESA sign the Gateway memorandum of understanding (I-Hab and ESPRIT contributions)
SpaceX Falcon Heavy chosen to launch PPE and HALO together (approx $331.8M)
NASA finalizes the $935M HALO contract with Northrop Grumman
UAE joins: MBRSC to build the Crew and Science Airlock, with an Emirati astronaut to fly to Gateway
HALO's primary structure lands in Arizona from Turin for final outfitting
Widespread corrosion found throughout HALO's primary structure after arrival
Ignition rollout: NASA announces it intends to pause Gateway in its current form and build a lunar surface base instead
Apr 2026
NASA issues a stop-work order on the HALO contract, then valued at $1.9B
ESA Council: I-Hab continues to critical design review, Lunar View slows, Lunar Link may join Moonlight; an interim ministerial in Italy in December 2026 to set Europe's course
NASA OIG interim memo ML-26-002: contract values for the four canceled Artemis elements grew from nearly $2.8B to $5.9B (estimated completion costs at least $8.1B); HALO stood at $1.9B at stop-work
Targeted late 2028
Launch of SR-1 Freedom, the Mars-bound nuclear electric spacecraft built around Gateway's repurposed PPE (as of September 28, 2026)
